### 1.1 Background

Our current rate limiting system uses an in-memory implementation (`SimpleRateLimiter`) that operates in-process only. This architecture has several limitations:

- State is lost on restart

- Cannot enforce global rate limits across multiple services
- Limited to 100 requests per window maximum

Build a distributed, fault-tolerant rate limiting system using Redis as the primary store with graceful fallback to in-memory limits for degraded scenarios.

|--------|--------|
| Throughput | 50,000 requests/second |
| Latency Overhead | < 5ms p99 |
| Availability | 99.9% uptime |
| Fallback Trigger Time | < 100ms |

### 1.4 Scope

- **In Scope:**
  - Redis cluster-based rate limiting
  - Per-user and per-IP rate limits
  - Dynamic configuration via configuration center
  - Fallback mechanism to in-memory limits
  - Migration tooling from legacy system

- **Out of Scope:**
  - Token bucket algorithm (using sliding window only)
  - Circuit breaker integration (Phase 2)
